newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech Bass unit says raises prices 4-5pct.
newsitem.headline: Czech Bass unit says raises prices 4-5pct.

text.p: Czech brewer Prazske Pivovary a.s., 55 percent owned by Britain's Bass plc, said it had raised wholesale prices by a below-inflation average of 4-5 percent from March 3.

"We have stated several times that it is vital to the continued survival of the Czech beer industry that beer prices are realistic. However, this change will not happen overnight," said Prazske Pivovary spokesperson Diana Dobalova in a statement.
Czech year-on-year inflation was 7.4 percent in January.
The Czech Republic boasts the world's highest per capita beer consumption but with average prices at around $0.33 (10 Czech crowns) per half litre profits are low.
Competition in the beer industry is extremely strong and breweries find it difficult to pass price rises on to customers.
Prazske Pivovary is the third largest brewing group in the country with a 14 percent market share.
